titulo: Power's out: stop opening the fridge
destinatario: se lo manda alguien que vivió un apagón a su amigo que abre la heladera cada diez minutos 'para ver si sigue fría', para decirle que cada vez que la abre gasta el tiempo
regla_guardable: Door shut: fridge up to four hours, full freezer forty-eight hours.
fuentes: CDC, Keep Food Safe After a Disaster or Emergency: up to four hours in a refrigerator if the door stays closed; full freezer forty-eight hours, half full twenty-four; appliance thermometer, forty degrees or below; never taste food to know if it is safe
USDA FSIS, Keeping Food Safe During an Emergency (same figures)

frases.texto: The power's out, and you keep opening the fridge to check on the food.
Every peek lets the cold out. Keep that door shut.
The CDC says a closed fridge keeps food safe for up to four hours.
A full freezer holds for about forty-eight hours. Half full, about twenty-four. Same rule: door closed.
Heads up: past those times, never taste food to check if it's safe. Don't test it with a bite.
The CDC says to keep an appliance thermometer in your fridge, so you can see if it stayed at forty degrees or below.
Do it today, before the next storm.
Send this to the friend who opens the fridge every ten minutes during a blackout.
